plain_claim: For every semantic bound B and closed-type property Φ: (1) a Boolean definition-site check C over open types that is both sound (DefCheckSound B Φ C) and instance-complete (DefCheckComplete B Φ C) exists if and only if Φ is substitution-stable relative to B (SubstStable B Φ); and (2) for any instantiation-witness map w satisfying HasInstWitness B w, the witness-evaluating check witnessDefCheck Φ w (defined without Classical.choice, and executable whenever Φ and w are computable) is both sound and instance-complete relative to B if and only if SubstStable B Φ holds.

hypotheses.name: hw : HasInstWitness B w (in witnessDefCheck_sound_and_complete_iff_substStable)
hypotheses.purpose: ensures w t supplies a B-conforming instantiation whenever t admits at least one B-conforming closed instance
hypotheses.witness_class: constant witness maps over 1-type-parameter open types under FullNoAlignBound

nonvacuity_witness: FixedConstNoAlignBound with constZeroNoAlignWitness and packedNoAlignWf, realizing both true and false verdicts
non_claims: The existential right-to-left construction in exists_sound_complete_defCheck_iff_substStable uses classical decidability over arbitrary Prop-valued bounds B; witnessDefCheck_sound_and_complete_iff_substStable gives one constructive route avoiding Classical.choice when an explicit witness map w satisfying HasInstWitness B w is supplied (specific bounds and properties can also admit direct syntax-directed checks such as naiveDefPackedCheck under FullNoAlignBound even when partial const indices rule out any t-independent constant witness map, hasInstWitness_neg_const_map_fullNoAlign).

DefCheckSound B Φ C and SubstStable B Φ quantify over environments (A, σ) where instTy A σ t = some τ succeeds; even when SubstStable B Φ holds and a sound, instance-complete check accepts t (C t = true), instantiating t at a B-conforming (A, σ) can still fail with instTy A σ t = none (and CollectRes.pmeError) due to partial const arithmetic (such as N - 1 at N = 0, cex_partial_sub_post_mono_error) or unresolved associated-type projections (instTy_neg_unresolved_proj).

DefCheckComplete requires C t = true whenever at least one B-conforming closed instance satisfies Φ; a sound conservative check sufficient for universal validity AllInstSat B Φ t (DefCheckSound B Φ C without DefCheckComplete B Φ C, rejecting mixed open types while accepting a sound class of universally valid ones) does not require SubstStable B Φ (for example, boundedDefPackedCheck in R4; see cex_defCheckSound_without_complete_not_substStable).

Open types that admit no B-conforming closed instance (for example, due to an always-failing const index 0 - 1) satisfy AllInstSat B Φ t and SubstStable B Φ vacuously, and witnessDefCheck Φ w accepts them when w t fails to instantiate t.

plain_claim: For every const-index expression e satisfying isCtorIdx e = true (acyclic constructor and parameter terms over canonical natural scalars, with no add, sub, or div nodes), instantiation-time evaluation in evalIdx never fails (IdxTotal e); and for any two index expressions e1 and e2 with isCtorIdx e1 = true and isCtorIdx e2 = true, semantic equality across all natural parameter valuations (IdxSemEq e1 e2) holds if and only if rigid syntactic AST equality e1 = e2 holds, which is decidable via DecidableEq IdxTerm.

hypotheses.purpose: excludes partial checked subtraction and floor division nodes; in the class of 1-const-parameter arithmetic index expressions, there is idxSub1 (N - 1) with isCtorIdx = false that fails evaluation at γ 0 = 0

hypotheses.name: h1 : isCtorIdx e1 = true (in idxSemEq_iff_eq_of_isCtorIdx)
hypotheses.purpose: excludes left-hand arithmetic expressions; in the class of 1-const-parameter total addition expressions, there is 0 + N paired with N that satisfies IdxSemEq while .add (.lit 0) (.cparam 0) ≠ .cparam 0

hypotheses.name: h2 : isCtorIdx e2 = true (in idxSemEq_iff_eq_of_isCtorIdx)
hypotheses.purpose: excludes right-hand arithmetic expressions; in the class of 1-const-parameter total addition expressions, there is N paired with N + 0 that satisfies IdxSemEq while .cparam 0 ≠ .add (.cparam 0) (.lit 0)

non_claims: Const parameters (.cparam i) range only over Nat scalars (γ : Nat → Nat, MonoKey.cnstArgs : List Nat), never over CVal.ctor trees, and function-call const argument evaluation (evalNatArgs in GenStmt.call) rejects every .ctor value with none (evalNatArgs_neg_ctor, triggering CollectRes.pmeError during collectAndCheck); IdxTotal guarantees non-failure of evalIdx inside OpenTy.arr, not admission of constructor terms as GenStmt.call const arguments.

DecidableEq IdxTerm tests rigid syntactic AST equality (treating .cparam i as universally quantified constants rather than unifiable metavariables). Unlike RFC 2000 (where each abstract const expression occurrence creates a distinct anonymous projection so even two separate AST occurrences of N + 1 do not unify) and stable Rust (where ADT const arguments and open const arithmetic require nightly feature gates), IdxTerm compares AST structure directly.
isCtorIdx is sufficient but not necessary for IdxTotal: total addition N + 1 satisfies IdxTotal while isCtorIdx (N + 1) = false (add_idxTotal_yet_not_isCtorIdx).

idxSemEq_iff_eq_of_isCtorIdx quantifies over all unconstrained valuations γ : Nat → Nat in IdxSemEq; under a where-clause fixing γ 0 = 4, .cparam 0 and .lit 4 agree on constrained valuations despite syntactic inequality (not modeled in IdxSemEq).

CVal models canonical pointer-free, padding-free, union-free value trees directly as an inductive tree; raw pointers with provenance, unions, and floating-point NaN non-reflexivity are outside the grammar.

In Toy.SubstStable, GenFn.pmeAsserts is attached to the function declaration rather than to GenStmt, so inline assertions on a reached function run in both includeMentioned = false and includeMentioned = true modes; GenStmt.deadBranch affects only callee traversal. For an instance k already known to be collector-reachable via Reachable (rather than IntrinsicReachable), pointwise isLocalFn P k = true suffices to transfer passesLocalPme to passesIntrinsicPme without crate-wide AllLocalMir (passesIntrinsicPme_of_passesLocalPme_of_isLocalFn); crate-wide AllLocalMir P T is needed once reachability is stated over intrinsic fn.body edges (cex_external_callback_local_pme_hole).
Says nothing when collectAndCheck returns .outOfFuel (for example, under polymorphic recursion; see monomorphization-reachability-lazy-shim-synthesis-and-closed-verification-targets R8 and R9).

design_question: Which monomorphic instances are certified to satisfy post-monomorphization assertions when crate collection succeeds under used-only versus mentioned-items traversal, and when does collector reachability match intrinsic call-graph reachability?

plain_claim: (1) On progDeadBranch (where fn 0 mentions fn 1::<u8> inside deadBranch), used-only collection (includeMentioned = false) returns .ok [⟨0, [], []⟩] while mentioned-mode collection (includeMentioned = true) reports .pmeError ⟨1, [tyU8], []⟩; (2) on progUnreachedLib, mentioned-mode collection from ⟨0, [], []⟩ returns .ok [⟨0, [], []⟩] with AllLocalMir, yet the unreached instance ⟨1, [tyU8], []⟩ is neither IntrinsicReachable nor Reachable and violates passesIntrinsicPme; (3) on progExtHole (where fn 1 has localMir = false), mentioned-mode collection returns .ok [⟨0, [], []⟩, ⟨1, [tyU8], []⟩] with passesLocalPme = true while passesIntrinsicPme is false on ⟨1, [tyU8], []⟩; and (4) on progExtCallbackHole (where local fn 0 calls external fn 1 which calls back into local fn 2), mentioned-mode collection returns .ok [⟨0, [], []⟩, ⟨1, [tyU8], []⟩] while local instance ⟨2, [tyU8], []⟩ (isLocalFn = true) is IntrinsicReachable, not Reachable, and violates passesIntrinsicPme.
nonvacuity_witness: concrete crate programs progDeadBranch, progUnreachedLib, progExtHole, and progExtCallbackHole
non_claims: In progExtHole, collectAndCheck inserts the external key ⟨1, [tyU8], []⟩ into the output list T with passesLocalPme = true (and in progExtCallbackHole truncates monoEdges at fn 1), whereas rustc_monomorphize::collector (collector.rs:137-139) creates no collector node when an external non-generic item's MIR is unavailable (and rustc exports generic MIR in .rmeta for cross-crate generic functions); progExtHole and progExtCallbackHole model a per-crate verifier or summary check that treats external generic calls as uninterpreted stubs without discharging their PME obligations or traversing their callbacks.

Statements after unconditional divergence (such as return or loop {}) that lower to unreachable zero-predecessor blocks before mentioned-items gathering are not modeled by deadBranch, and the Rust Reference (r[expr.block.const.not-executed]) leaves dead-branch const evaluation unspecified.

Model–system relation: none proved. These are statements about the toy model; they neither establish nor refute the corresponding claims about rustc, the Rust language, zerocopy, or any program verifier.

design_question: What is the modularity and cross-crate price of enforcing safety invariants via post-monomorphization assertions instead of definition-site trait bounds?

plain_claim: (1) As an elementary corollary of DefCheckSound and R1, for every bound B, property Φ, and check C satisfying DefCheckSound B Φ C, Φ evaluates to true (and hence Φ τ1 = Φ τ2) across all B-conforming closed instances of every C-accepted open type t, and if C also satisfies DefCheckComplete B Φ C then SubstStable B Φ holds globally; (2) for every B_src, B_assumed, Φ, C, generic function fn, and openTarget, BoundEntails B_src B_assumed transfers DefCheckSound B_assumed Φ C to DefCheckSound B_src Φ C, and when BoundEntails (DeclBounds.sat fn.bounds) B_assumed and C openTarget = true hold, GenericBodySafeUnconditional fn openTarget Φ holds; (3) assuming an unstated bound (FullNoAlignBound when source declares emptyBounds) makes naiveDefPackedCheck on Packed<T0> violate both DefCheckSound and GenericBodySafeUnconditional for packedNoAlignWf at substAlign16; and (4) PME-guarded fnTransmuteLike on (.prod (.tparam 0) (.tparam 1)) satisfies GenericBodySafeUnderPme for eqProdByteSize yet violates GenericBodySafeUnconditional without a PME-admission precondition.

hypotheses.name: hSound : DefCheckSound B Φ C / DefCheckSound B_assumed Φ C
hypotheses.purpose: the check C must be sound under the assumed bound; in the class of 1-parameter packed open types under emptyBounds, there is naiveDefPackedCheck accepting Packed<T0> while violating DefCheckSound, accepted-type invariance, and GenericBodySafeUnconditional

hypotheses.name: hComp : DefCheckComplete B Φ C (in second conjunct of defCheckSound_accepted_true_and_substStable_of_complete)
hypotheses.purpose: conservative sound checks need not imply global SubstStable; in the class of 2-type-parameter packed open types under DeclBounds ⟨[0], []⟩, there is boundedDefPackedCheck ⟨[0], []⟩ which is DefCheckSound and accepts Packed<T0>, yet fails DefCheckComplete while packedNoAlignWf fails SubstStable

hypotheses.name: hEntails : BoundEntails B_src B_assumed / BoundEntails (DeclBounds.sat fn.bounds) B_assumed
hypotheses.purpose: call sites enforce only the source-declared bound; in the class of 1-parameter generic functions with emptyBounds vs. FullNoAlignBound, there is naiveDefPackedCheck on Packed<T0> at substAlign16 violating both DefCheckSound and GenericBodySafeUnconditional
hypotheses.witness_class: 1-type-parameter generic functions with emptyBounds vs. FullNoAlignBound

hypotheses.name: hAccept : C openTarget = true (in genericBodySafeUnconditional_of_defCheckSound_of_boundEntails)
hypotheses.purpose: C must actually accept openTarget; in the class of 2-type-parameter generic functions with bounds ⟨[0], []⟩, there is openTarget = Packed<T1> rejected by boundedDefPackedCheck ⟨[0], []⟩ that violates GenericBodySafeUnconditional

nonvacuity_witness: source bound DeclBounds.sat ⟨[0, 1], []⟩ entailing assumed bound DeclBounds.sat ⟨[0], []⟩ with sound check boundedDefPackedCheck ⟨[0], []⟩ accepting Packed<T0> (and rejecting Packed<T1>), paired with (FullNoAlignBound, naiveDefPackedCheck) witnessing DefCheckSound and DefCheckComplete
non_claims: defCheckSound_accepted_true_and_substStable_of_complete, defCheckSound_of_boundEntails, and genericBodySafeUnconditional_of_defCheckSound_of_boundEntails are elementary definitional corollaries of DefCheckSound, BoundEntails, and R1 (GenericBodySafeUnconditional fn openTarget Φ unfolds directly to AllInstSat (DeclBounds.sat fn.bounds) Φ openTarget and does not inspect fn.body).

Sound generic-IR reliance on a definition-site check (DefCheckSound B Φ C) does not require SubstStable B Φ when C is conservative rather than instance-complete (¬ DefCheckComplete B Φ C): for example, boundedDefPackedCheck ⟨[0], []⟩ is DefCheckSound under DeclBounds.sat ⟨[0], []⟩ while failing DefCheckComplete and SubstStable (cex_defCheckSound_without_complete_not_substStable; likewise under emptyBounds via boundedDefPackedCheck_sound and packedNoAlignWf_not_substStable_emptyBounds).

ClosedTy.byteSize omits inter-field and trailing alignment padding (.align 16 tyU8 has byteSize = 1, byteSize_ignores_align_and_padding), and fnTransmuteLike paired with eqProdByteSize isolates the equal-byte-size PME obligation only—omitting alignment compatibility (PmeCheck.alignLe), alignment-rounded size, bit-validity (FromBytes/IntoBytes), and immutability required for sound reference transmutation.

Does not prevent a generic-IR verifier from verifying PME-guarded generic functions conditionally under an explicit PME-admission premise (GenericBodySafeUnderPme, matching PolymorphicConditionalVerification in anneal-pme-mir-semantics-and-polar-ctfe-admission); cex_pme_guarded_fn_unsound_without_pme_assumption refutes only unconditional generic safety (GenericBodySafeUnconditional) that omits PME admission.
Does not claim any defect in Aeneas, Charon, Creusot, Verus, or any existing generic-IR verifier.

Model–system relation: none proved. These are statements about the toy model; they neither establish nor refute the corresponding claims about rustc, the Rust language, zerocopy, or any program verifier.

design_question: Which compiler or verifier checks may a verifier capturing generic IR soundly rely on, and what happens if it assumes unstated bounds or ignores post-monomorphization assertions?

plain_claim: (1) As a definitional List.all equivalence for verifier-executed post-capture checking, for every associated-type environment A, closed-type property Φ (whether substitution-stable or not), target map targetOf, and captured monomorphic instance list T, checkMonoTarget A Φ targetOf T = true holds if and only if MonoCaptureCertifiedOn A Φ targetOf T holds; and (2) for every mode includeMentioned, crate program P, root list roots, fuel, output list T, and target map targetOf, when collectAndCheck includeMentioned P roots fuel = .ok T, AllLocalMir P T holds, and HasPackedPmeGuard P targetOf T holds, MonoCaptureCertifiedOn P.assoc packedNoAlignWf targetOf T holds.

hypotheses.name: hOk : collectAndCheck includeMentioned P roots fuel = .ok T (in monoCaptureCertifiedOn_of_collectAndCheck_ok_of_packedGuard)
hypotheses.purpose: collection must succeed without pmeError; in the class of 1-function local packedWf-guarded crates, there is progMonoPacked at root ⟨0, [align16U8], []⟩ where AllLocalMir and HasPackedPmeGuard hold, collection fails with pmeError, and MonoCaptureCertifiedOn fails
hypotheses.witness_class: 1-function local packedWf-guarded crates instantiated at an over-aligned argument

hypotheses.name: hLoc : AllLocalMir P T (in monoCaptureCertifiedOn_of_collectAndCheck_ok_of_packedGuard)
hypotheses.purpose: external items with localMir = false skip local PME evaluation; in the class of 1-function external crates, there is Pext at root ⟨0, [align16U8], []⟩ where collectAndCheck returns .ok and HasPackedPmeGuard holds, yet MonoCaptureCertifiedOn fails
hypotheses.witness_class: 1-function external-MIR crates instantiated at an over-aligned argument

hypotheses.name: hGuard : HasPackedPmeGuard P targetOf T (in monoCaptureCertifiedOn_of_collectAndCheck_ok_of_packedGuard)
hypotheses.purpose: each captured function must declare PmeCheck.packedWf for targetOf; in the class of 1-function unguarded local crates, there is Punguarded at root ⟨0, [align16U8], []⟩ where collectAndCheck returns .ok with AllLocalMir, yet MonoCaptureCertifiedOn fails
hypotheses.witness_class: 1-function local crates omitting the PmeCheck.packedWf guard

nonvacuity_witness: progMonoPacked under emptyBounds (where packedNoAlignWf is unstable) captured at [⟨0, [tyU8], []⟩, ⟨0, [tyU64], []⟩]
non_claims: checkMonoTarget_iff_monoCaptureCertifiedOn characterizes a direct verifier-side check over T (requiring no compiler PME), whereas monoCaptureCertifiedOn_of_collectAndCheck_ok_of_packedGuard transfers compiler PME collection solely for PmeCheck.packedWf / packedNoAlignWf (not .sizeEq, .alignLe, or .idxValid); when roots = [] (an uninstantiated library crate), collectAndCheck returns .ok [] and MonoCaptureCertifiedOn holds vacuously over T = [].

MonoCaptureCertifiedOn certifies only the captured instance list T; uncaptured instantiations k ∉ T (such as ⟨0, [align16U8], []⟩ on progMonoPacked) are not certified and can violate Φ (cex_monoCapture_without_collectOk).

Does not by itself prove that T is closed under runtime calls unless paired with a closed-target collector theorem (see monomorphization-reachability-lazy-shim-synthesis-and-closed-verification-targets R1 and R2).
